gen_risks.description: Institutional fragmentation and weak coordination among multiple transport ministries and agencies may cause implementation delays and inefficiencies.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish clear inter‑agency coordination mechanisms, regular joint NPSC meetings, define roles and responsibilities, and use a centralized project coordination unit.
gen_risks.evidence: Key challenges ... institutional fragmentation, insufficient funding, and capacity constraints. Multiple agencies operating with overlapping responsibilities (Sectoral Context, paragraph 15).

gen_risks.description: Insufficient long‑term financing for operation and maintenance of bridges, roads and market facilities after project closure could erode benefits.
gen_risks.mitigation: Create sustainable financing mechanisms (road fund, market user fees), embed O&M budgets in annual work plans, and train local councils on revenue collection.
gen_risks.evidence: Critical Assumptions state funding is available for maintenance; RMFA collected only US$12.5 M, a small fraction of needed support (Sectoral Context, paragraph 15).

gen_risks.description: Climate‑induced flooding and landslides may damage newly built bridges and roads, reducing service life.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply climate‑resilient design standards: oversized drainage, scour protection, flood‑proof deck heights, and conduct detailed hydrological modelling before construction.
gen_risks.evidence: Climate change expected to exacerbate flooding, landslides ... risks to bridges, roads and markets (Country Context, paragraph 10) and designs will follow climate‑proofed parameters (Component 2 description).

gen_risks.description: Procurement capacity gaps in the PCIU (no procurement unit, limited staff knowledge) risk delays, non‑compliance and fraud.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit qualified procurement specialist before effectiveness, conduct regular procurement clinics, use STEP for tracking, and strengthen bid evaluation committees.
gen_risks.evidence: PCIU does not have a procurement unit currently and it will be established and staffed... (Procurement section) and procurement risk assessment lists PCIU as not established (Annex 6).

gen_risks.description: Weak financial management capacity; FM risk rated high due to limited experience with World Bank procedures.
gen_risks.mitigation: Centralize FM unit, hire FM specialist, provide targeted FM training, implement FM manual, and conduct periodic internal audits.
gen_risks.evidence: FM risk before mitigation is “High” mainly due to insufficient experience ... overall weak control environment (Annex 7).

gen_risks.description: Delay in establishing the National Project Steering Committee within 60 days may weaken oversight and coordination.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set a monitoring checklist, assign responsibility to MTA to convene NPSC within 30 days, and report status to the World Bank.
gen_risks.evidence: Legal covenant: Recipient shall establish a National Project Steering Committee no later than sixty (60) days of the Effective Date (Legal section).

gen_risks.description: Gender‑based violence and sexual harassment on public transport could undermine safety objectives and deter female users.
gen_risks.mitigation: Install CCTV on buses, create a SH hotline, run awareness campaigns, and train operators on response protocols.
gen_risks.evidence: Component 1 sub‑component c mentions CCTV to reduce harassment; gender section outlines SH action plan (Gender aspects).

gen_risks.description: Low mobile‑phone penetration among rural women may limit uptake of the AMIS mobile app, reducing market information benefits.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide alternative channels (radio, community meetings), partner with women’s NGOs for outreach, and deliver training on app use.
gen_risks.evidence: Rural women have limited phone access; internet penetration 21.2 % (Component 3 description, paragraph on mobile access).

gen_risks.description: High road‑safety risk; Sierra Leone’s poor safety record may lead to accidents during construction and operation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement road‑safety training, improve signage, enforce speed limits, integrate safety audits into RAMS, and monitor incidents via the road‑safety database.
gen_risks.evidence: Sierra Leone has 33 road crash fatalities per 100 000 population, third highest in West Africa (Transport Connectivity, paragraph 8).

gen_risks.description: Activation of the Contingent Emergency Response Component may be delayed by procedural bottlenecks, limiting rapid disaster response.
gen_risks.mitigation: Finalize CERC manual before implementation, conduct simulation exercises, pre‑approve trigger criteria, and keep standby funds readily accessible.
gen_risks.evidence: Component 5 description of CERC includes a manual and emergency action plan (Component 5).

gen_risks.description: Cost overruns common in the region; climate‑resilient designs may increase capital costs beyond budget.
gen_risks.mitigation: Include a contingency reserve, apply value‑engineering, monitor expenditures via STEP, and adjust scope if necessary.
gen_risks.evidence: Sensitivity analysis assumes a 25 % increase in capital costs; 43 % of projects in Sub‑Saharan Africa experience >15 % overruns (Economic Analysis, paragraph 9).

gen_risks.description: Extreme weather during the rainy season could halt construction activities, causing schedule delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Schedule critical works in the dry season, use modular construction methods, and build weather‑contingency buffers into the timeline.
gen_risks.evidence: Construction will use incremental launching to avoid delays from prolonged rainy seasons (Component 2 description) and wet season regularly disrupts connectivity (Country Context, paragraph 2).

gen_risks.description: Private‑sector lease‑operate‑own bus scheme risk of operator default or inability to meet lease payments.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct rigorous credit assessments, require performance bonds, monitor lease payments regularly, and include step‑in rights for the government.
gen_risks.evidence: Component 1 sub‑component c describes lease‑operate‑own scheme and private capital enabling (Private Capital Facilitation section).

gen_risks.description: Market infrastructure may be under‑utilized if not aligned with farmer needs, reducing expected economic returns.
gen_risks.mitigation: Carry out participatory needs assessments, involve farmer groups in design, monitor usage, and adjust facilities based on feedback.
gen_risks.evidence: Needs assessment will adopt participatory processes, collect gender‑disaggregated data, and prioritize women’s perspectives (Gender aspects, Component 3).

gen_risks.description: Governance and corruption risk in procurement and contract award could lead to fraud and loss of value for money.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce transparent bidding, publish award notices, use independent audits, implement anti‑corruption training, and monitor via STEP and CRPD.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement risk assessment lists fraud, collusion, weak complaint redress; anti‑corruption guidelines apply (Annex 6 and Annex 7).

gen_risks.description: Limited capacity of SLRA to operate the Bridge Management System may delay asset‑management benefits.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide BMS training, develop user manuals, allocate dedicated staff, and pilot the system before full roll‑out.
gen_risks.evidence: Component 2 sub‑component c supports development of a digital bridge management system (BMS) and technical assistance includes software and user guidelines (Component 2).

gen_risks.description: Inaccurate or delayed data feeding into AMIS could mislead farmers, reducing the platform’s effectiveness.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish data‑quality protocols, conduct regular verification, train data collectors, and maintain a manual backup reporting system.
gen_risks.evidence: Limited capacity to integrate wide variations of value chains and inadequate resources for timely data collection (Component 3 description).

gen_risks.description: Delay in recruitment of key project staff (procurement specialist, FM specialist, social specialist) could postpone procurement and financial processes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Start recruitment early, use competitive selection, appoint interim staff if needed, and set firm recruitment timelines with performance incentives.
gen_risks.evidence: PCIU will recruit a procurement specialist, FM specialist, internal auditor and social specialist before project effectiveness (Implementation Arrangements).

gt_risks.description: Political and governance is rated Substantial. This project's activities are not highly sensitive to moderate perturbations in the political dispensation, although pronounced degeneration in political stability could still undermine their implementation. The more likely risk is that poor governance may affect implementation for the road sector, resulting in reduced commitment during implementation.
gt_risks.mitigation: These risks will be mitigated through close supervision, strict adherence to the criteria for beneficiary selection, and fiduciary oversight.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risk is assessed as Substantial. Sierra Leone's post-pandemic recovery was disrupted by concurrent domestic and external shocks. Inflation and exchange rate depreciation reached record levels, depressing economic activity and triggering a severe cost-of-living crisis. Fiscal accounts have deteriorated on account of macroeconomic headwinds and policy slippages, and risks to debt sustainability have intensified. The economy is projected to grow at 3.8 percent on average during 2023-2025, below the long-term trend, and this baseline is vulnerable to downside risks given recent fiscal slippages and expenditure overruns. The macroeconomic risk may raise concerns about contractors' cost overrun and delay of payment.
gt_risks.mitigation: Key macroeconomic reforms will help reduce the imbalances and avoid the downside risks. The project is 100 percent financed by IDA which will help mitigate the macroeconomic challenges to project implementation.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk is rated Substantial. The key fiduciary risks are related to the overall governance context of the project, the risk that procurement of project works may be delayed and/or result in higher-than-expected bid prices or poorly performing contractors, and difficulty retaining qualified procurement and FM professionals in the PCIU.
gt_risks.mitigation: These risks will be mitigated by implementing an action plan that aims to strengthen the accountability and control framework for project implementation and improve overall fiduciary performance, and by ensuring adequate procurement and FM training. The PPSD will establish appropriate prequalification requirements and adopt standard lessons from experience procuring similar works contracts in Sierra Leone. The FM risk will be further mitigated by recruiting an internal auditor under PCIU.

gt_risks.description: The project's E&S risk is Substantial (para 74, explicitly pointing to section V.D for detail - para 74 states both environment risk and social risk are rated Substantial 'as indicated in section V.D'). Section V.D (paras 64-68): overall E&S risk classification is Substantial, with eight of ten Environmental and Social Standards (ESS) applying. Environmental risk is Substantial: construction activities are expected to generate air/noise nuisance, construction waste, and traffic/worker safety issues, and Component 2 in particular could affect downstream water users (water quality/hydrology, navigation, fish catch, riparian vegetation), with some impacts potentially long-term or irreversible (e.g. accidental spill of used oil/electrolytes/hazardous materials into the river during construction). Social risk is also Substantial: key risks include physical and economic displacement of boat/ferry operators, loaders, and traders after bridge construction; SEA/SH risks from the contractor workforce; elite capture in market-infrastructure interventions; social exclusion of vulnerable groups (persons with disabilities, women/small traders, the landless, elders); and secondary risks including potential child labor, communicable-disease spread from the contractor workforce, and local conflict over benefit-sharing from downstream impacts.
gt_risks.mitigation: Standard measures per the ESIA/ESMP to be prepared for project activities, including energy-efficiency measures per World Bank EHS Guidelines/GIIPs; a site-specific SEA/SH risk assessment and commensurate GBV/SEA/SH action plan; the Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP) and Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), disclosed April 19, 2024; hiring a social specialist with GBV/SEA/SH experience before project effectiveness; an ESIA and Resettlement Action Plan/livelihoods restoration plan already under development for the seven originally-planned bridges, with updated ESIA/ESMP/RAP and a SEA/SH action plan to be disclosed within one month of effectiveness; and a functional grievance mechanism (GM) plus Labor Management Procedures (LMP) for project workers.
